steps: This video shows how to route A P I errors by severity, so the right ones wake people up. First, TicketFlow goes live on bring your own cloud in your A W S account, so data stays in-region.
A TicketFlow call to messages create hits the rate limit, and Claude returns a rate limit error, status four twenty nine.
A retry loop bug resends the failed call immediately, again and again. Each retry gets another four twenty nine, and the errors start to spike.
Monitoring groups the errors by cause and rates the four twenty nines as a warning. The right response to a rate limit is to log it and back off, not to page anyone.
The warning reaches you, not the pager. You trace the spike back to the retry loop.
Your backoff fix runs through the C I C D pipeline, with tests, evals and security scans, then ships. TicketFlow now backs off on four twenty nine.

Only a four oh one authentication error would page on-call, because that needs a human. The four twenty nines never woke anyone. The takeaway: severity decides who hears about an error. The full walkthrough is in the Gennoor Claude certification course.
